Hi Sana / procurement team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick follow-up with a concrete inputs checklist so we can produce a focused dedicated-capacity recommendation and SLO map for the deal. If you can confirm the items below we’ll return a slot-by-slot GPU plan + expected p95 latency and tokens/sec headroom.

Assumptions we plan to evaluate (please correct where needed):
- Model family: Llama 2 13B (8-bit quantized) as the primary serving candidate; fallback to Mistral-7B quantized for lower-cost tiers.
- Average request composition: prompt (user + system) ~140 tokens, expected generated response ~220 tokens (total ~360 tokens per request).
- Traffic profile: baseline steady QPS ~15 r/s, peak bursts up to 95 r/s (30 minute peak windows), daily active hours 8am–8pm PT.
- SLO target: p95 end-to-end response <= 700 ms for 90% of calls; p99 < 1.5s as negotiated.

Requested confirmations:
1) Typical prompt+response token counts (or sample traces).
2) Peak sustained RPS and worst-case burst RPS.
3) Acceptable fallback behavior (e.g., degrade to smaller model or queue).
4) Any compliance constraints for Private deployment (if we need on-prem/VPC).

Next step: once we have numbers from you, we’ll produce a one-page compute plan that maps tokens/sec -> GPUs, with headroom and canary rollout suggestion. I’ve attached a lightweight workbook template we’ll fill out.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30m sizing call if that’s faster.

—

1) Token sizes: our initial telemetry (pilot) shows median prompt+response ~240 tokens but with a long tail; median 240, mean ~370. We’ll attach sample traces.
2) Traffic: baseline currently ~18 r/s, expected steady state after launch ~35 r/s. Peak daytime bursts (clinical hours) historically reach ~110 r/s for 10–25 minute windows. Night/weekend quiet.

Thanks — that’s really helpful. Based on your telemetry and our serving benchmarks I ran a quick conservative mapping (workbook attached). Key outputs below — these are baseline proposals to discuss:

Summary of inputs we used (conservative):
- Model: Llama2-13B (8-bit) equivalent throughput measured on rtx-a6000 / A100-40GB kernels with Redwood runtime.
- Effective tokens per request (use 370 tokens).
- Target p95 latency: two scenarios (500 ms aggressive, 700 ms default).
- Peak burst target: 110 r/s sustained for 15 minutes; steady-state 35 r/s.

Compute math (simplified):
- Tokens/sec at steady-state = 35 r/s * 370 t = 12,950 tokens/sec.
- Burst tokens/sec = 110 r/s * 370 t = 40,700 tokens/sec.
- Measured single GPU sustained token throughput (Redwood runtime, 13B quantized): ~6,500 tokens/sec at p95 ~650 ms under mixed request sizes with continuous batching. (This is conservative — we report median higher but design for p95.)

Sizing conclusions:
- Steady-state needs ~2.0 GPUs (12,950 / 6,500 = 1.99).
- To meet 110 r/s burst with ~40% headroom and keep p95 <= 700 ms, we recommend a slab of 7 GPUs (40,700 / 6,500 = 6.26 -> rounded to 7).
- If you require p95 <= 500 ms target, measured tokens/sec per GPU drops (more aggressive scheduling) to ~4,500 t/s -> burst requires ~10 GPUs for comfort.

Recommended dedicated configuration (two options):
A) Balanced (recommended for initial commit): 4-GPU reserved slab + autoscale burst up to 8 GPUs. Rationale: reduces committed spend while enabling managed burst to 8 GPUs for typical peaks; expected p95 ~600–750ms during largest spikes (depends on batchability).
B) High-SLO (if 500 ms p95 is contractual): reserve 8 GPUs slab (no more than +/- 1 GPU autoscale) to reduce queuing and ensure p95 ~450–550ms.

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- Autoscaling speed: we can pre-warm kernels so cold-start impact is <200ms but scale-up time for new GPUs depends on region and capacity — recommend burst buffer (2 GPUs) always-on.
- Caching: enabling prefix/KV caching for repeated clinical prompts can reduce observed tokens/sec by 8–20%. We’ll estimate savings in the attached workbook.
- Fallbacks: queueing + controlled degrade to Mistral-7B keeps clinical correctness easier to audit; we’ll add guardrails in rollout.

I attached the spreadsheet with the per-minute token math, cost estimates and a two-scenario slab plan. Next steps: 1) Confirm which SLO target (500 ms vs 700 ms) you prefer; 2) We’ll prepare a committed-capacity proposal (monthly slab + burst policy) and an SLA appendix for procurement.

Quick ops note to add to Camila’s plan — from the runtime/ops side: 
- Tail latency mitigations: we recommend a hybrid queueing window (100–300ms) + best-effort batching. That reduces GPU contention on bursts and keeps user-space timeouts predictable.
- Canary strategy: start with 2-GPU pilot on dedicated pool routed for 5% of traffic; measure p95 and cache hit benefit. Increase reserved commit after 2 weeks if p95 < target.
- Security/compliance: for VPC deployment we’ll include KMS integration and extended audit logs; Jordan will follow up with the SOC2 artifacts.

Happy to review the workbook with your infra/procurement team on Thursday if that helps.
